identity.author: Perpetua, Saturus, and the Redactor
identity.edition: Gebhardt, Acta martyrum selecta (1902), Passio SS. Perpetuae et Felicitatis

source_text: Cum adhuc, inquit, cum prosecutoribus essemus et me pater uerbis auertere et deicere pro sua affectione perseueraret: Pater, inquam, uides, uerbi gratia, uas hoc iacens, urceolum siue aliud? Et dixit: Video. Et ego dixi ei: Numquid alio nomine uocari potest quam quod est? Et ait: Non. Sic et ego aliud me dicere non possum nisi quod sum, Christiana. Tunc pater motus hoc uerbo mittit se in me, ut oculos mihi erueret; sed uexauit tantum, et profectus est uictus cum argumentis diaboli. Tunc paucis diebus quod caruissem patrem, domino gratias egi, et refrigeraui absentia illius. In ipso spatio paucorum dierum baptizati sumus; et mihi spiritus dictauit non aliud petendum ab aqua nisi sufferentiam carnis. Post paucos dies recipimur in carcerem: et expaui, quia numquam experta eram tales tenebras. O diem asperum! Aestus ualidus turbarum beneficio, concussurae militum. Nouissime macerabar sollicitudine infantis ibi. Tunc Tertius et Pomponius, benedicti diaconi qui nobis ministrabant, constituerunt praemio ut paucis horis emissi in meliorem locum carceris refrigeraremus. Tunc exeuntes de carcere uniuersi sibi uacabant: ego infantem lactabam iam inedia defectum; sollicita pro eo adloquebar matrem et confortabam fratrem, commendebam filium; tabescebam ideo quod illos tabescere uideram mei beneficio. Tales sollicitudines multis diebus passa sum, et usurpaui ut mecum infans in carcere maneret; et statim conualuit et releuata sum a labore et sollicitudine infantis, et factus est mihi carcer subito praetorium, ut ibi mallem essem quam alicubi.
english: While we were still with our guards, she says, my father kept pleading with me in words, trying out of his love to turn me aside and bring me down. I said, Father, do you see this vessel lying here, for instance a little pitcher or something else. He said, I see. I said to him, Can it be called by any name other than what it is. He said, No. So I too cannot call myself anything other than what I am, a Christian. Then my father, stung by that word, flung himself at me as if to tear my eyes out, but he only hurt me, and he went away defeated, with the devil's arguments.

Then, because I was without my father for a few days, I gave thanks to the Lord, and I breathed again in his absence. In that stretch of a few days we were baptized, and the Spirit prompted me to seek nothing from the water except endurance in the flesh. A few days later we were taken into prison, and I was terrified, for I had never known such darkness. O harsh day. Fierce heat from the crowd, the shoving of the soldiers. And last of all I was worn thin with anxiety for my baby there. Then Tertius and Pomponius, the blessed deacons who were attending to us, arranged by a payment that we should be let out for a few hours into a better part of the prison and catch our breath.

Then, coming out of the prison, everyone attended to his own need, while I nursed my baby, who was already faint from hunger. Anxious for him, I spoke to my mother and I comforted my brother and I entrusted my son to them, and I pined away because I saw them pining away on my account. Such anxieties I endured for many days, and I obtained leave for the baby to remain with me in prison. At once he recovered his strength, and I was lifted from the burden and anxiety for my baby, and suddenly the prison became a palace for me, so that I would rather have been there than anywhere else.
